search_queries: targeted PyPI and PyPI Stats lookups for 11 named TOML packages
uncertainty: Bounded TOML search captured 2026-11-17: 1 query, 100 recorded hits (100 unique), at most 100 per query; the PyPI Simple index has no relevance order and the name filter matches unrelated names, so the leads come from targeted lookups. Three third-party paths pass both valid controls with exact hand-written typed trees, parser-scoped coverage and AFL++ feedback, three identical runs per control each: tomlkit 0.15.2 (591,365,129 PyPI Stats last-month downloads; 845 package lines, 408 in parser.py; controls differ by 401 AFL++ tuples), tomli 2.5.0 (263,305,223; 284 lines, 259 in _parser.py; controls differ by 137 tuples) and rtoml 0.14.0 (1,380,894; source-built PyO3 extension with Rust LLVM coverage: 768 toml_parser 1.1.5 lines, 488 underlying toml 1.1.8 lines; controls differ by 1,242 AFL++ tuples over the toml, toml_parser and toml_datetime crate sources). tomli is the same code family as the standard tomllib API (a vendored copy), so the two are not independent; the hand-written trees are tomli's independent check. Only tomli's pure-Python wheel is measured, not its mypyc-compiled wheels. tomlkit is an independent style-preserving parser; its downloads mostly reflect Poetry and other tool installs. rtoml shares the Rust toml_parser family with the selected Rust toml and toml_edit paths (the same toml_parser 1.1.5 release); it is measured as a coverage-instrumented source build, not the official wheel. toml 0.10.2 (145,147,540) fails typed-scalars: it drops the fractional seconds of the local time 00:32:00.25. pytomlpp 1.1.0 (43,243; C++ toml++ via pybind11) and toml-rs 0.4.3 (18,062; Rust parser from a git branch via PyO3) give both exact typed trees, but their parsers are compiled native code; they stay leads until a source build with native coverage and AFL++ instrumentation exists. pytoml 0.1.21 (337,081) rejects the hexadecimal integer and qtoml 0.3.1 (2,002) the fractional-second offset date-time of typed-scalars. The standard tomllib API passed both controls on a host run. Two valid controls establish only the tested TOML 1.0.0 subset; malformed input, huge documents and TOML 1.1 features are untested.
